rv.q: Black’s greatest gift is his ability to raise everyday, ordinary, even banal issues to the level of life-altering impact, distilling a story, an incident, even a life into three succinct minutes.
In its exemplary construction and performance, From the Heart offers a masterclass of songwriting that succeeds in sharing Black's joy of life with us.
Overall, this was a poignant and heartwarming production which held my attention from beginning to end.
From The Heart is a very pleasant 80 minutes, although it sometimes feels like a show mounted more for friends and family rather than West End audiences.

This version of From The Heart at the Garrick Theatre is perfectly judged: flawless vocals, comic sketches, moments of reflection, and effortless performances bring together Don Black’s storied career in an evening of unbridled joy.
At just 80 minutes, From The Heart is a lovely little show filled with powerhouse vocals and technical excellence.
With its outstanding cast, understated staging and abundance of warmth, From the Heart is a thoroughly delightful evening of musical storytelling.
From The Heart succeeds in exactly what its title promises: a joyous evening created with evident passion by a lyricist whose words continue to resonate across generations.
Warm, polished and consistently well performed, 'From the Heart' offers both an affectionate portrait of its subject and a rewarding evening of song.
That minor quibble aside, it is a superlative evening of entertainment.
Don Black's From The Heart is a joyous celebration of a lyricist who clearly loves his craft and, in his words, never stopped dreaming to finally lead to his own West End event.
It is 80 minutes of absolute perfection.
From The Heart is an evening of glorious cabaret that celebrates the musical love of one of our finest lyricists!
From the Heart is a joyful reminder of why we love live performance.
From The Heart is an 80-minute, joyous evening fuelled with sharp comedy, heartfelt ballads, and energetic performances, showcasing Don Black's passionate and talented career.
From the Heart is a lyrical, theatrical treat that deserves to be seen and heard.
It is a privilege to be in the audience, sharing the celebration with him.
For all this, the London scene should welcome the return of From The Heart with open arms.

cn.t: Critics warmly embrace this joyful celebration of lyricist Don Black's career, praising its intimate cabaret charm and stellar performances. While some note it's more new material than greatest hits retrospective, most find it a delightful, moving tribute.
